title: Zeschau (Dresden) to Seebach (St Petersburg), ciphered despatches 1841-1843 (HStAD 10731 Nr. 12)

steps.what: Fetched R5005-R5008 images from DECODE with the session cookie.
Listed every Dresden key record on DECODE; latest is 1799-1806, none for the 1840s. No printed edition found.
Hand-transcribed R5005 in full from line strips (70 lines, 3,764 digits; recorded as 3,969 until 11 Nov 2026, a miscount).
Pair counts, null-digit sets, prefix-code lengths, per-line phase by EM.
Homophonic annealer on a synthetic 1,800-letter French text.
Homophonic letter annealer on pairs (both phases) and two prefix codes.
Enhanced the rubbed pencil glosses: 'la pre m i er e' over 11 70 82 34 29 40, 'que' over 46.
Syllabary annealers seeded with the gloss values (free, one-cell, length-neutral).

Contributed by Brice Dudout (PR #401): variable-length segmentation of R5005, proposed by an LLM on the text without blocks a3 and a7: the first digit(s) set the group length (0x/1x and [3468][13468] = 2 digits; [2579]x[13468] = 3; 00xx/55xx/77xx = 4), groups run on across lines. 1,309 groups, 190 types, 15 outside the forms.

Contributor's pre-registered single measure on the held-out blocks a3+a7 (859 digits): 291 of 296 groups in the forms (0.983, bar 0.95), against maxima of about 0.70 for digits shuffled within lines, pairs shuffled, and a synthetic true-pair homophonic cipher. Structure only; no value tested.

Integration check: segment.py re-run (output identical); held-out share recomputed with an independent script (291/296 = 0.983; secondary checks as stated); shuffle controls re-drawn (means 0.64 and 0.62, maxima 0.71 and 0.69 of 1,000). Not checkable: the blindness of the proposer and the pre-registration hashes. Digit count of R5005 corrected from 3,969 to 3,764; repeat counts corrected.

outcome.method_basis: R5005 was transcribed and attacked ciphertext-only; the rubbed-out pencil glosses show a table of letters and syllables and give a few values, and the digits were segmented into groups of 2, 3 and 4 (Brice Dudout, 11 Nov 2026, confirmed on held-out blocks), but no key and no reading resulted and no 1840s Dresden key exists on DECODE.
outcome.notes: Structure identified (groups of 2, 3 and 4 digits; letters and syllables) and five values proposed from the glosses; the September solvers ran on pairs and did not test this segmentation. Needs a solver on the groups, the key, imaging of the erased pencil, or the sibling letters transcribed.

credits.note: R5005 segmented in variable-length groups of 2, 3 and 4 digits (rule proposed by Fable 5.2), confirmed by one pre-registered measure on held-out blocks a3+a7 (98.3% in form vs 70% controls); see dudout/

prior.where: Contemporary interlinear pencil decipherment, now rubbed out and mostly illegible

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded. 11 Nov 2026: Brice Dudout (contributor, PR #401) had an LLM propose a segmentation rule on R5005 without blocks a3 and a7 and had a second agent measure it once on those blocks under a pre-registered protocol (dudout/validation.md).
